messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] methylkit unite function error
parts:
it seems there are duplicated coordinates in the methylRaw object. You need to find out where they are, sometimes you can remove the duplicates. I can not tell you why this happens without seeing a reproducible example. It could be from methylation calling most likely. You can try methylDackel or Bismark methylation callers to see if that resolves the problem

Best,
Altuna

Hello. First of all, thank you very much for your answer. 
My name is JunHyuk Shin  and I am currently studying for a master's degree at Seoul National University. 
And to be more specific, I read the data directly from sam file. 
I made a methylrawlist. 
And the location information of the processor is used as readtranscriptfeatures function. 
I read the cpgi and shore information using readfeatureflank function. 
But the promoter section uses the region count function to compare with each other.
We created a corresponding methylrow list and created a method file using the Unite function. 
I used the getmethyldiff function and it worked well without any problems. 
But I also want to compare the proportion of Cpg Island, so I did the same procedure. 
No execution. One difference is that location information for cpgi is used by readfeatureflank function. 
And in fact, if you look at the data form, if you look at the first few lines alone, there's a difference here. 
I think that's the problem because the strand part is uniformly identical. 
I wonder what you think about this.
Also, the guide pdf says that you can compare the promoter region with the cpgi region, but details are not given
so I wanted to make sure that i did everything correctly or is there different way to do this ?   


2019년 6월 19일 수요일 오후 7시 2분 39초 UTC+9, Altuna Akalin 님의 말:

it seems there are duplicated coordinates in the methylRaw object. You need to find out where they are, sometimes you can remove the duplicates. I can not tell you why this happens without seeing a reproducible example. It could be from methylation calling most likely. You can try methylDackel or Bismark methylation callers to see if that resolves the problem

Best,
Altuna
